queries.text: How did American cities change across four decades (1980-2024): gentrification, inequality, affordability, and displacement — every claim cited?
Median household income by city for 1980, 2000, and 2024
Share of households earning less than half the median income (poverty rate) by city for 1984, 1994, 2004, and 2014
Gini coefficient or Theil index measuring income inequality within metropolitan statistical areas for 1979-1983, 1989-1993, and 1999-2003
Average asking rent per square foot in major US cities for 1985, 1995, 2005, and 2023
Median sale price of single-family homes in designated gentrifying neighborhoods versus non-gentrifying neighborhoods from 1980 to 2020
Percentage change in the share of households spending more than 30% of income on housing by city between 1984 and 2022
Number of displaced residents or evictions recorded annually in specific urban districts during periods of rapid property value appreciation from 1990 to 2015
Change in racial composition (percentage of White vs. Black/Hispanic residents) in census tracts classified as gentrified between 1970, 1980, and 2000

search_hits.title: Gentrification in America
search_hits.snippet: Governing analyzed Census tract data for the nation's 50 largest cities. Portland (58.1% of eligible tracts), Washington D.C. (51.9%), Minneapolis (50.6%), and Seattle (50%) led; nearly 20 percent of lower-income neighborhoods gentrified since 2000, compared to 9 percent in the 1990s; poverty rate percentage-point change -0.7 gentrifying vs +6.7 not gentrifying.

search_hits.title: Urban Gentrification Metrics: Four Decades of American City Transformation (the exemplar report)
search_hits.snippet: The operator's exemplar report (vendored as source-report.pdf): New York City leads with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469 versus the national average of 0.40 in 2013, while Atlanta and Miami follow at 0.57 and New Orleans at 0.56; the Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 (+225% since January 2000); 48 of the 50 largest metros saw worsening mobility with Houston the sole improvement (+1.1%).

search_hits.title: Gentrification by the numbers
search_hits.snippet: UGA real estate professor Richard Martin: 'I found a very large, across-the-board increase in the amount of gentrification in the 2000s relative to earlier decades' — gentrification levels were at their lowest in the 1970s and increased every decade until 2010.
